entries.question: What is swimrun?
entries.answer: Swim, run, repeat: a race that alternates between open-water swimming and trail running, in one go, with the same gear all the way.
entries.more: Teams of two (or soloists) move over a course that alternates between open-water swimming and trail running, in one go, with the same shoes and gear all the way.

entries.question: But can tigers actually swim?
entries.answer: Yes, they can actually swim really well. Wikipedia: "The tiger is a powerful swimmer and easily transverses rivers..." Tigers are among the few big cats that enjoy water.
entries.more: They cool off in it and swim across rivers. That is why a tiger is our swimrun mascot, and why the tiger in the logo is mid-swim.

entries.question: How many segments does a swimrun have?
entries.answer: It depends on the race: from a handful of swims and runs to dozens.
entries.more: A short course may have a handful of segments, a big island-hopping race has dozens. TigerLegs counts them for you: upload a GPX and it lists every swim and run segment.

entries.question: What are the distances in swimrun?
entries.answer: There are no standard distances, and that is on purpose: a course follows whatever islands, rivers or lake crossings are possible and pleasant in an area.
entries.more: Wikipedia lists categories of short and long courses, but those are relatively arbitrary. The Ötillö World Championship in Sweden (Stockholm archipelago) is about 60 km of running and 9 km of swimming, definitely one of the longer courses. Het Rondje Eilanden is far shorter, with about 1,500 m of swimming and running in total. Courses with 10 run and 10 swim segments are common. That is exactly why measuring segments per course is useful.

entries.question: Do you swim in your running shoes?
entries.answer: Usually yes. Most swimrunners keep their shoes on while swimming.
entries.more: They often use paddles and a pull buoy, plus a wetsuit that is easy to run in. More in our Substack series 'From zero till Ötillö': https://from0tillotillo.substack.com/

entries.question: What does TigerLegs stand for?
entries.answer: Terrain Informed Gpx ExtractoR: LEts Go Swimrun!

entries.question: Is my GPX file uploaded to a server?
entries.answer: No. You choose the file in your browser, and the analysis runs there; the file stays on your device and nothing is sent to a TigerLegs server. Terrain data from OpenStreetMap is opt-in, and then only a coarse bounding box and your IP address go to OpenStreetMap's Overpass service, never your trackpoints. See the About page for details.
